text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor My first introduction to the board game of Sorry was in the early 60's. Sorry was one of the more fast and fun games. The object of the game is to be the first player to move all 4 of your men around the board to get back home. You choose from 4 different colors of your men and your home- blue, green, yellow or red. There is a deck of cards that tell you how many spaces to move your man, and of course it isn't as easy as just moving your man as quickly as you can around the board to get home before anyone and win the game. There are obstacles along the way, should a player get to slide, he slides everyone in his way back to start, and no two men can occupy the same space, so someone has to go back to start- Sorry!

I remember when we played with 2 players, the game took about 15-20 minutes, but with 4 players, it took close to half an hour. It's very fast moving and even faster when hardly any players are sent back to start. I really love the look of this classic 1939 Sorry Game- it's a little different from the one we played on in the 60's. Regardless of the look you like, Sorry is a fast and fun game that brings back so many fun memories of when we had 15 minutes to kill before we went bike riding to a picnic on a lovely summer day in 1962. This early version of the game is really a nice one to own and it also comes with other game versions you can play including a Sorry For One, in case you have a few minutes to kill by yourself! Some Classic games never wear out their fast fun and this 5 Star Classic Sorry Board Game is one of them!
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor [[VIDEOID:c9ed210fcea7bd15ff238268da66c6e5]] I really liked this classic game of Sorry. I hadn't played this game in over 25 years, so this is a fun blast from the past.

The game isn't as silly or as random as I remember it. For a random move your pawn game, there is actually a decent amount of strategy involved.

The rules were a bit confusing, since they used the old 1959 rules. Here's my summary of the rules: You can only move your pawns out of start if you pick a 1, 2, or sometimes a Sorry card. If you get a 1 or a 2, then you only move out to the first circle. You only slide when you get on the first part of the slide. If you can't move, you don't move, and you need an exact count to get into the Home square. Follow the rest of the instructions on the cards.

Pros:
+It's possible to win no matter how far behind a player is
+Great rendition of a classic game
+A lot of fun
+Great for any ages

Cons:
-The rules are a bit confusing. I had to clarify some of the rules on the internet.
-The game starts out very slowly
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

Mainstreet Classics Dutchman 3-in-1 Combo Folding Board Game Set The board is a very nice, stained wood. It measures 15.75" by 15.75" (including the handles) wide by 1" deep when open or 2" when folded. It folds in half, with the recessed backgammon side holding the game pieces during storage. Two pairs of magnets hold the board closed when folded. The magnets have been effective at holding the set closed without being difficult to open when desired. The top board is 8 by 8 squares across. The wood checkers are just under 1" across and have a slight protrusion on the bottom to keep them in place when a piece is crowned. There are 15 pieces each of brown and white, and these pieces are also used for backgammon. The wood chess pieces are common, simple chess shapes and have a felt bottom. The included game instructions are brief and not really enough to learn to play the games, but it's easy enough to find this information online. From the box: "Solid wood travel set accented with walnut, maple, and mahogany playing surfaces" as well as the California Prop 65 warning with "Wash hands after use."

There are some 1 star reviews for this set, and I have a hard time believing it's for the same set. The set I got has lovely workmanship and everything looks sturdy and well-made. text_fidelity_a:
Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules This is the best deck building game EVER!!
I am in my 20's and have only recently been introduced to deck building games, and instantly fell in love.
DOminion and the DC Comic deck games are my favorite, but Dominion provides a larger variety because the cards used change.
The game its self comes with several possible versions of the game.
For example, the game is plaid with several action card decks to draw from, but Dominion comes with twice as many action cards. So, no game is exactly alike. The rule book comes with various options of which action cards to play with for certain kinds of games.
This game is dynamic!

I first played Dominion at a bar with board games. After a few times I fell in love and bought this second edition. The cards are beautiful, more colorful than the first edition. (I attached some photos to see to see the cards)

It says that the game can be played in about 30 minutes... for me it takes closer to an hour with 3 players. It also probably depends on what type of game you play (which actions cards to choose to play with) But because we are still learning, maybe we go a little slower, constantly re reading what the action cards say/do.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.
text_fidelity_b: Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules

text_fidelity_a:
Sagrada - Board Game by Floodgate Games, 4 playres The game is fun, kind of like solving a sudoku puzzle where there's some limited interaction between players. Some people take too long to make decisions, don't play with someone like that in a group of more than 2 people as there's not much to do while waiting your turn. The game is pretty and well built, and the dice drafting mechanic is unique and fun.

I'm glad I bought the game and it's in our rotation, but it's not as good as games like Patchwork or Carcassonne because you're always trying to do the same thing- fill up your grid while maximizing your score. Patchwork has shifting objectives you need to play off against each other. Carcassonne has more interplay between people while building out the map and has more emergent complexity. We pull this game out mostly because we have 3 people and want the fun of the dice drafting game mechanic.
text_fidelity_b: Sagrada - Board Game by Floodgate Games, 4 playres

text_fidelity_a:
Grey Fox Games Deception: Murder in Hong Kong Board Game, Fast Pace Murder Mystery, 20 min, 4-12 Players, Age 14+ ...Who Among You Can See Through The Lies or is Capable of Not Getting Caught This is a murder-mystery game for a crowd that doesn't require any acting. It's much more akin to a social deduction game like Resistance, but with a few different elements.

In Deception, each player gets a combination of 8 cards in front of them: 4 weapons and 4 "clues" - really just random objects. One player is given the role as murderer, and another player knows who that player is, and it is that second player who gives clues to everyone else using clue boards, each of which involves placing a marker on one of five different words. This player does not talk other than to provide a "no" in case of a wrong answer.

The game is good, but doesn't ever hit the next level for me, and it's really because of the clue boards and cards. So many of these objects are very benign things that don't ever see any specific clues. One time, the murderer chose a toy, specificially the toy duck card, and it was my job to attempt to communicate this to the other players. Unfortunately, not one clue card that came up over the course of five different rounds had anything to do with fun, ducks, birds, toys, or any other words of that nature, and that means that the players ended up rather frustrated with me for not giving them anything to go on in terms of guessing the clue. This happened rather frequently, enough that we decided to put this one away after a few tries.

When it works, it's very fun. When it doesn't, it feels rather frustrating. I thought it worked more than it failed, and the components are pretty nice, so I give it the edge from 3.5 to 4 stars, but I am not 100% sure that I'll keep it in my collection.

Adult warning: A game subtitled "Murder in Hong Kong" might not seem like it requires a parental warning, but I know that I was playing Clue and other similar games as a child, and as a parent of a young gamer who is willing to try anything, I feel it necessary to include a warning. Some of the cards in this one are illegal drugs, and the clue cards do use more "intense" words to describe elements of the crime. Oftentimes, figuring out the whodunnit of this one requires you to think pretty hard about how certain weapons might be used to kill someone, so it's not for the young ones out there.
text_fidelity_b: Grey Fox Games Deception: Murder in Hong Kong Board Game, Fast Pace Murder Mystery, 20 min, 4-12 Players, Age 14+ ...Who Among You Can See Through The Lies or is Capable of Not Getting Caught

text_fidelity_a:
CUTE STONE Pretend Play Kitchen Sink Toys with Play Cooking Stove, Pot and Pan with Spray Realistic Light and Sound, Dish Rack & Play Cutting Food, Utensils Tableware Accessories for Kids Toddlers I bought this sink for my son and was at first really excited based on the reviews. It was very easy to put together and get the water running through the sink. It has really cute utensils and food that you can “cut.”

However, we have been through replacing the first sink and I am in the middle of returning our second sink because both times the stove top stopped working after just a few minutes of play.

It seems there is a faulty design inherent to the toy where if you get water inside the sound component it will start to misfire and won’t stop making noise and won’t turn off.

I came downstairs the other morning to the sound of the burner on when I know we didn’t leave the toy on. I took the back off and I noticed that water was trapped in the circuit board. Terrible design for a toy that is literally a sink.

I want to like this because my son was so excited about this toy but I’m afraid back to Amazon it will go so we can pick out something higher quality.
text_fidelity_b: CUTE STONE Pretend Play Kitchen Sink Toys with Play Cooking Stove, Pot and Pan with Spray Realistic Light and Sound, Dish Rack & Play Cutting Food, Utensils Tableware Accessories for Kids Toddlers

Monopoly Board Game The Classic Edition, 2-8 players I have many fond memories of playing "Monopoly" with siblings, cousins, and parents when I was child and then with my own family as an adult. This version is very close to the version I remember playing in the 70s. The game board and tokens are sturdy, and my favorite tokens from when I played as a kid are included - the dog, the horse, and the race car, along with the shoe, hat, thimble, iron, wheelbarrow. Two others are included that I don't remember at all - a cannon and a ship.

The game comes with rules for the standard, full length game. Players choose a token and go around the board purchasing property and building houses and hotels, hoping to force their opponents into bankruptcy. This game can be played by two or more players.

The property title deeds are still made of thin cardboard, but may be a little more flimsy than older versions. The money tray is even better than it used to be. It's made of plastic and seems like it will hold up much better than the old flat tray with the flimsy dividers that used to quickly fall apart. The only thing that is off for me is the color of the Community Chest cards. They are a yellow-orange color instead of the yellow I am used to. I don't know if the very first version of the game had cards this color or not, but this is the first time I've seen this.

If you're looking to replace your old game or haven't played the original version, you can't go wrong with this classic game.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Board Game The Classic Edition, 2-8 players

So far, I've made the two types of dogs (it's a head swap, really) and it works really well. Instructions are easy to follow and the pieces fit together easily. This would probably be a good kit for children ages eight and up..if they're a good reader, probably younger would do fine. The kit uses three different power methods: battery pack, capacitor, and solar power. I tried all three and they each worked just fine. Of course the capacitor worked better than solar, and the battery pack absolutely demolished the others in terms of performance. If the model can support it, I would likely use the capacitor for most things. It is very easy to recharge using the battery pack as well.

I can't wait to put together some of the other bots with my youngest. He's a big fan of building things. Thumbs up!

Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game We just aren't overly fond of this game. It ended up being super frustrating for us.

When you first open the game, you have to put the game board together. This takes a bit of time, but it's not too bad. It looks nice enough, and I like that the game board is thick and sturdy. My boys love the whole idea of the game, and I don't think we've ever played a game where the board stood up. That was really cool! Our biggest issue is how difficult it is to keep the climbers in place. They're constantly falling when they shouldn't be. My children are 3, 5, and 8, so that may have a great deal to do with it. Keeping those climbers hanging where they should proved impossible for us, though. It's also a little frustrating that each player has to move around to play. The game board only faces one way, and you can't move it without making the climbers fall off(even more). That means when 4 people are playing, you can't just sit in a spot and enjoy the game. You have to move around, depending on whose turn it is. That might not be a big deal for many, but it frustrated my little guys.

Overall, we really like the whole idea of the game, and the fact that the game board stands up, but it ended up being incredibly frustrating for everyone.

text_fidelity_a:
Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors The Alias is potentially a great example of the new generation of quadcopters with electronic flight control boards that provide six axis stabilization. When their transmitter control levers are properly trimmed at the beginning of each flight they will hover very stably and are easy to fly even for a beginner.

Unfortunately, LaTrax and Traxxas (LaTrax makes the product and Traxxas provides all customer support) released the Alias before they found a good quality motor that works properly with the Alias. Since the Alias uses four motors and is inoperable if any one of the motors fails this is a major problem.

My Alias flew great for the first two days, but then it became very unstable and flew unpredictably. After only the the sixth or eighth flight one of the motors failed and the Alias would not fly at all.

Traxxas told me the Alias does fly unpredictably when one of its motors is weakening and getting ready to fail. They said they would send me a free replacement motor, but so far it has not arrived. Looking at other Amazon reviews, and on the internet, I see that many other people have also had very early motor failures. I strongly recommend people should not buy the Alias until LaTrax and Traxxas have figured out the early motor failure problem, presumably by finding a better motor.

Update: January 14, 2014

After two initial days of use before one of the motors broke, I have been unable to fly my new Alias for two and a half weeks now. Traxxas keeps saying they will send me a new motor as soon as the most recent batch they received "gets through quality control". I fear I have wasted $150 to buy the Alias.

Update January 20, 2014

After three weeks Traxxas finally sent me a replacement motor ....drum roll.....however, they sent the wrong motor! Traxxas checked their records, agreed they had sent the wrong motor, and promised to send the correct motor. I am pleased they are trying to provide good customer service, but I am now in my fourth week without being able to fly my otherwise excellent Alias after one of its motors broke on the second day after I opened it at Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors

text_fidelity_a:
Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game The predecessor to this game, Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, is my all-time favorite game, and holds a high place on my game shelf despite being a “one and done” experience. Does this new iteration hold up to the high standard the previous game established?

To start with, the production value on this new version is heads and shoulders above the 2013 edition of SHCD that I own. The paper is printed on much nicer stock, the box is thicker and better designed to hold the contents, and the instruction manual in particular shows a great attention to detail that the previous edition lacked. I particularly like that in this edition, the solutions to each case are printed upside down in the back of the box, and that the solutions are encased in an envelope secured to each case book to prevent spoiling any aspects of the story with erroneous page turns.

Like the previous game, this “board game” is much more of a “choose your own adventure” story for you and your friends to solve. Each case is represented by a book, in which you’re given an introductory story, and then allowed free reign to investigate a variety of leads and allies to assist you in gathering information about whodunit. Once you think you know what’s happening, turn to the questions and find out what happened in this story – don’t worry, there are significant explanations and story to give closure to each case.

This is a stand-alone game, meaning that if you haven’t already played the original SHCD, you can purchase this with no strings attached. I don’t think I would recommend that for new players, however.

Jack the Ripper and the West End Adventures are quite different from what you get in the original game. In the original, there were some threads of story that remained from one case to the next, but in the new version, four of the cases are designed to be played campaign-style in an effort to solve the Jack the Ripper murders.

I’m sure that there will be many people out there who love the Jack the Ripper campaign - a set of four cases that are thematically tied together that will allow you to hunt down Jack using a separate map and additional investigative helpers – but it really isn’t for me. First of all, the cases are quite a bit darker and less whimsical than your traditional Sherlock Holmes story and case, and are tied together only by the fact that they occur in the same area and time period. I think the original cases are too difficult to be played by, let’s say, a 10 year old, but the stories wouldn’t be inappropriate for them in terms of language and description. The Jack cases, on the other hand, would carry a definite R-rating – they’re well-researched historically, and include lots of graphic description and a few cuss words as well. If you know anything about the historical Jack cases, you’d probably know this going in, but if you’re used to the style of the original cases, know that this is a darker affair. Secondly, you absolutely cannot find Jack and get a satisfactory conclusion until the fourth case, which is a decent investment in time with little return for parts 1 - 3. Third, and this is the big reason I didn’t like it, is that the mini-mysteries you’re solving in parts 1, 2 and 3 are not mysteries at all, but historical backstory. The questions are answered directly by particular sources, so if you visit the right allies and pursue the right leads you will simply be given the correct answers to each piece without putting much of anything together outside of remembering what the leads gave you. This was a very different experience, with a different writing style, different thematic elements, and a wholly different style, and since I am such a fan of the tried-and-true SHCD formula, I did not enjoy it as much as others may.

The other six cases are all stand-alone cases, and are quite good, although in most cases, they’re quite a bit harder than the already difficult cases in the original box. Like that set, some are better than others, but I will admit that the overall quality of these cases is on-par with what came in the original box, but still harder. I don’t think this is the right place to start with the SHCD universe.

Therein lies the only real problem that I have with this SHCD set – that while packaged as a stand-alone, this game is put together in a way that strongly suggests that it’s a sequel. If you think of it in movie terms, sure, you can watch most sequels without seeing the original movies, but why would you, especially if you know going in that watching the original is going to improve your experience? The cases in this box are more difficult, and the Jack the Ripper set is an odd starting place.

Overall, this game comes very highly recommended to any fan of the original set of cases. If this game sounds like something you’d be interested in, get it, but be advised that I think that the original set of 10 cases are a superior starting place.

4.5/5
text_fidelity_b: Sherlock Holmes Consulting Detective: Jack the Ripper & West End Adventures Standalone Game

text_fidelity_a: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32" Purchased one of these without exactly knowing what I was buying. Sure, I knew it made noise - but didn't know how it did that or what it might sound like ( guess I could have looked on YouTube, but I didn't). Anyway, now that I've got one it's all everyone wants to play with. Basically it's a short tube with a thin piece of taut plastic covering one end (think tiny drum head), and a long loose spring mounted to the center of the plastic. Holding the tube and shaking it causes the spring to vibrate like springs do, those vibrations travel up to the drum head and the sound reverberates into the tube and is amplified out the other end. Makes for some pretty interesting sound effects. Overall I'm more than happy with my purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary) I bought 2 of these blasters for my daughter and I. We have Nerf battles in the house and She wanted a semi auto (to back up her Recon and Maverick) and I need a backup for the Hail Fire. This is a clip system balster with a fly wheel launcher (need 4 AA batteries). All in all I'm pretty pleased.
Good: This blaster does a lot of things well. It is a semi-auto (requires 4 AA batteries), but does not feel heavy or unbalanced. Easy to shoot 1 handed and can be double wielded. Clip system is nice as we have a lot of extra clips so reloads are fast. The clip release button has a good positive feel and has not accidentally relesed a clip yet. The blaster has a top and bottom tactical rail and will accecpt a stock and barrel extention (although why you would want to do this is questionable as it takes away the intent of this compact blaster). Handgrip is comfortable but may be to small for XL hands. Accel. button has a good feel to it. There are 2 place for sling attachment and both spots are logical! Battery door is a sigle screw affair. Accuracy is better than expected (I can hit a human size target 5 out of 6 times at a 30 foot range). Battery life has been good and Rechargables offer no problems.
Bad: This blaster has more safety switches than a modern Table Saw! There is the jam door switch, the clip sensor switch, dart sensor switch, voltage switch (regulator), accel trigger switch, and probably others that I haven't come across yet. The main trouble maker is the dart sensor switch. It works great until the last dart in the clip. Sometimes the dart pressure is not enough to press the switch arm so the blaster won't fire the last dart (VERY ANNOYING!) The easiest NONE WARRENTY VOIDING fix is to open the jam door, take a thin (about 1/8" wide) piece of duct tape (about 2 inches long) and tape the switch to the top of the reciever. I taped it up and around the body and out the top of the jam door. After aprox 100 shots the tape is still holding and I have yet to have a dart left in the clip. The gun is also prone to jamming if you pull the trigger slowly. When firing off a dart you need to make sure to pull the trigger crisply. This only seems to be a problem on the first shot (probably because I usually empty the clip after that first shot). Another problem I've seen is the dislike this blaster has for non-elite darts. If your first dart in the clip is a streamline version you can almost be assured a jam (funny that it only happens if the non-elite is in the first position on the clip- load it farther down and it fires like any other dart). Honestly if your gonna use this for any formal matches stick to the Elite darts. Range is about 35 to 40 feet- hard to get any further.
Final thoughts: This is truely a fun blaster. It does have a few kinks to it, but nothing that a little duct tape can't fix. It is compact enough to carry as a secondary blaster, but combined with additional clip options (I'm thinking an 18 with a couple six back-ups) this could be a close quarters primary blaster. At the current $20 this is really a no brainer.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary)

NERF Laser Strike 4 Player Lazer Tag Pack - Indoor or Outdoor Game for Girls, Boys, Families, and Adults - Includes 4 Blasters with 300 ft Range, 4 Vests, and 4 Holsters These are super cool and fun. And I like playing as an adult, too, although only if the kids want to play. I love that there are so many slight adjustments you can make - with or without the chest plates, changing ammo types, etc., and especially that it takes more than one shot to kill, since it really sucks when you get out right away and have to wait for the next round.

I know other people have said this, but the battery thing just kills me. I mean, any down time makes me see all those batteries draining prematurely. Yeah, you could get external rechargeables, but those Ni-MH or other nickel types really aren't quite the right type for something where you want to recharge them every time. I know it would cost more, but if these all had a li-ion internal and a docking station for the set, it would be perfect. I mean, it's already a fairly expensive toy, so why not offer the option at least. I mean, I have a lot of batteries around, but 24 at once is a lot. And then if just one guy dies, you have all kinds of sadness going around.

Even so, great set when everything is up and running.

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

There is an app that you download to your phone, and using that app, you can view your LEGO set, and watch it move and change a little bit. The app itself is downloadable on iTunes and Android, and works well on the Android system, although you really likely want to use a phone because of the size of the tablet. Like all parents, I'm not entirely thrilled about yet another excuse to hand over my phone, but I think that the augmented reality piece is really more of a gimmick that my daughter will tire of sooner rather than later. The building of the set must come first in order for this to work, and that's mildly educational, and we get to play with the LEGO set without the phone as well.

And did I mention how cool this set is, even without the augmented reality? The ghost theme makes for some cool pieces, and I like how this one looks when it's done. It's a winner.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue We enjoyed using this kit. I did it mostly with my 7 and 10 year old children. My 7 year old was the most interested. My 5 year old had interest, but he wasn't as gentle with it as he needed to be.

I especially like that the projects are centered around a story. You read a little, then build, read, build..... It makes the whole thing more fun and puts things into perspective. Everything you need is provided in the box, except for 2 AA batteries(so have those on hand before starting). The projects can get a little complicated, particularly when the gears come into the story, but it's not too bad. Some children might need help(or it can simply be a challenge to see if they can figure it out on their own).

The quality is mostly nice. The treehouse is made out of sheets of wood, and it seems durable to me. It won't last through rough play, but for the project, it holds up well. When building the treehouse, you can glue the pieces into place. We chose to take it apart, so we could do the projects again later with my youngest child. (Untying the knots was a bit of a pain, but otherwise, it's pretty simple to take apart.) There are a few pieces that are paper, though, and these are much less durable.

If you're looking for a fun project for a rainy day of learning, this is a nice kit to try.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue

Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck My boys love this thing! They are 1(average for age) and 4(very small), but they are about the same size. It's the perfect size for both of them, but it is on the small size. I don't think it will be too long before they get too big for it. Of course, another little will be right behind them to give it more use!

They have so much fun with it, of course I recommend it. But, there are a few MINOR negative issues I have with it.

-Keep the instructions initially! Getting that handle attached is more difficult than it would seem. Also, you want to have some strong hands close by to push in the wheels. It was extremely hard for me to get them to pop in. I do admit my hands are pretty weak, and I am an exhausted pregnant momma. The average person might not have trouble with them, but I'd be on the safe side. :)

-There are little velcro strips on the bottom that is suppose to keep the cloth in place. It doesn't work for us. It keeps coming loose as the boys play, and we have to constantly reattach it. Thankfully, it's not long enough to drag the floor too bad, so it doesn't create a tripping hazard.

-My boys do tip off the back a good bit while riding. Since it's so small, it has never caused them harm. They jump back up and keep playing. I do think it surprised them the first couple of times, but they are used to it by now. It might not be the best toy for really young children just learning coordination, though.

Overall, despite my small complaints, I still think this is a great toy that will provide lots of fun!
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck

The most fascinating thing is that this could be considered a "smart" train set - there is a sensor built into the tunnels so that once the train goes through, it can perform an action like stop, or sound horn. Adds an extra level of interactivity to the set, versus just having it go around in a circle.

The only concern of course is the hefty price tag. It's not cheap, but if you're gearing up for a big birthday bash, this could be the right choice!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Tech Sound Action Tunnel Deluxe Set

text_fidelity_a:
Hot Wheels Color Shifters Playset (2-Pack) Mattel has combined 2 Hot Wheel Play Sets into one with this Sharkport Showdown Megapack. Five cars are included, making this set lots of fun. Putting the set together is easy with the enclosed directions. It's basically snapping plastic pieces together. There are a few stickers you put on first that give more detail and color to the set.

Once you get the set together, you will see that the set needs water. This means a water mess as the cars dive into the tanks to change colors. For inside play, I put down a cheap plastic tablecloth on the floor, with a towel nearby. This made indoor play a much more dry experience, keeping the water contained to the plastic cloth. But for the best experience, with no water to clean up- outdoors is best when weather permits it.

The Sharkport Set has 2 color change zones (cold and warm), along with a big mouth shark that chomps a car when the car hits the trigger. To release the car from the jaws of the shark, another car must come to the rescue, by hitting the shark. The boys ages 3 to about 7 find this set lots of fun. The other set- The Splash & Dash Set is simply a dunk tank for color changing the cars. It has a hidden trap door, so the car makes a splash.

You will find that having hot wheel tracks (NOT included) attached to this set, makes this set way more fun, as the boys love zooming around the tracks with the 5 included cars before getting eaten by the shark or getting the cars color changed. There are a couple tips I found, to make the experience better also. Don't over fill the water tanks. Also you will find the cold water gets warm quickly and the warm water cools down just as quick. This means you will have to constantly keep emptying and refilling the 3 water containers with warm and cold water, unless you do what I do.

I put some ice into the cold water tanks. The cold water stays good longer and the color changes instantly, as the ice does the trick. When the water is no longer icy cold, the colors do not change on the cars. As for the hot water, I also found out I can deal with that too, as I keep hot water in a thermos and let the kids add the water. NOT TOO HOT- just hot enough for children to handle. Between the thermos and ice- they are good to play for hours- and they do!

Sometimes the cars jam or get lint on the wheels, but these are minor fixes with a little push or cleaning the tire areas with a toothpick. Overall, if you use a thermos of warm water and ice in the cold water- they won't be running back and forth to the faucets making messes and will have lots of fun changing these 5 car's colors and of course they love those shark bites too. This is a fun, but messy set that the boys enjoy when you know how to set it up with your plastic cloth, ice and thermos.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Color Shifters Playset (2-Pack)
